predecessors.note: The Zhao line restored by Zhao Xie. The old Zhao (ea-01 zhao) ended in 222 with the fall of Dai; the Eighteen Kingdoms table calls this state 'Zhao, briefly called Dai'.

land.text: Zhao Xie's Zhao and Chen Yu's Dai in 205: the Dai lands plus Changshan taken from Zhang Er

successors.note: Han Xin conquered Dai and Zhao in October-November 205. Zhang Er was then made King of Zhao (204 on the Timeline page, 203 on the Zhang Er page) as a Han vassal; that kingdom has no dossier.

capitals.name: Julu
capitals.note: 'Zhao Xie and his forces had retreated to Julu' under the Qin siege; the court's seat in the field. Qin held Handan, 'the Zhao capital'. Coordinates are the modern Julu county, not on the page.

capitals.name: Dai (Yu County, Hebei)
capitals.note: Not on any page opened: the seat of the Kingdom of Dai is given from the zhao dossier (ea-01), which places Dai at modern Yu County, Hebei. Unverified; Chen Yu governed Dai through its prime minister Xia Yue (Jingxing page).

rulers.name: Zhao Xie
rulers.title: King of Zhao; King of Dai from 206; King of Zhao again in 205
rulers.note: The year he became king is on no page opened. Killed at Xiangguo by Han Xin after Jingxing: 'Han Xin then pursued king Zhao Xie to Xiangguo and killed him there.'

rulers.name: Chen Yu
rulers.title: King of Dai
rulers.note: 'Zhao Xie rewarded Chen Yu by making him the king of Dai'; Chen Yu 'left the governance of Dai to its Prime Minister Xia Yue' and was killed on the Zhi River.

correction.text: Zhao Xie's rebel Zhao around Julu in central Hebei, 208-207, before it became Dai

keyframe_review.note: Shape unchanged (25,569 km2; 142 grid cells, 82 percent of them in Hebei, none in Shanxi), but it is not the Dai: the Eighteen Kingdoms table gives Dai 'northern Shanxi and northwestern Hebei', and 88 of these cells lie in Cliopatria's Chang-shan shape of 206, the Zhao core. The Battle of Julu page has Zhao Xie's forces besieged at Julu in 208-207, with Qin holding Handan; this is that rebel Zhao. The page gives no boundary or area.

ledger.note: 208: Zhao Xie's Zhao stands in central Hebei. Page silent on when and by whom Zhao Xie was made king; the Battle of Julu page has him ask 'for aid from King Huai II of Chu' and retreat to Julu. The year is Cliopatria's first year for the shape.

region.text: Zhao Xie's rebel Zhao around Julu in central Hebei, 208-207, before it became Dai

ledger.note: 208: Qin attacks Zhao. Zhang Han took 'Handan, the Zhao capital', and Qin 'ordered his deputies Wang Li and She Jian to besiege Julu'; 'In the twelfth month of 208 BC, Xiang Yu personally led an army across the river' to relieve it, so the siege began in or before 208. The page gives no month.

region.text: Zhao Xie's rebel Zhao around Julu in central Hebei, 208-207, before it became Dai

ledger.note: 207: the Qin army is beaten at Julu. Timeline page, 207 BC: 'A coalition rebel army led by Xiang Yu defeats Qin forces led by Zhang Han at the Battle of Julu'; the Julu page dates Zhang Han's surrender to 'the summer of 207 BC'.

206: Xiang Yu makes Zhao Xie King of Dai. 'The Kingdom of Dai (代), which was given to Zhao Xie, the erstwhile King of Zhao' (Zhang Er page, 206 BC); the Eighteen Kingdoms table: 'Zhao, briefly called Dai', ruler Zhao Xie.

region.text: central Hebei, the Zhao core carved out for Zhang Er

ledger.note: 206: the Zhao core goes to Zhang Er. Upon the fall of Qin 'the Kingdom of Zhao was split into two' and Changshan was 'given to Zhang Er' (Zhang Er page). The region is Cliopatria's Chang-shan shape; the page names no boundary.

ledger.note: 206: the Kingdom of Dai in the north. Eighteen Kingdoms table: Dai, Zhao Xie, 'northern Shanxi and northwestern Hebei', created by Xiang Yu in 206 BCE. The region is Cliopatria's 206 shape.

ledger.note: 205: Chen Yu takes Changshan and restores Zhao. 'In 205 BCE, Chen Yu, believing that his merit was equal to that of Zhang Er' attacked Changshan with Tian Rong's force; Zhang Er 'went to Hàn instead'. The Eighteen Kingdoms footnote: 'In 205 BCE, Changshan was destroyed, and Zhao was restored with Zhao Xie as King of Zhao'. The Timeline page has the conquest in 206.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary of the Zhao or Dai lands; Cliopatria's shapes are approximations.

notes: WHICH STATE: Cliopatria's 'Dai' (208-204) mixes two things. Its 208-207 shape (central Hebei, 25,569 km2) is Zhao Xie's rebel Zhao at Julu, and 88 of its 142 grid cells lie in the later Changshan shape; its 206-204 shape (57,016 km2) is the Kingdom of Dai of the Eighteen Kingdoms. The Eighteen Kingdoms table names the state 'Zhao, briefly called Dai' with the same king, so one dossier keeps the Zhao line (as the ea-01 zhao notes expect). It ends in October 205 at Han Xin's conquest, not in 204 where Cliopatria ends. The dossier of the old Zhao (zhao, to 222) is a different state and 'dai' of 228-222 (Prince Jia) is a different Dai. The Han-vassal Kingdom of Zhao of Zhang Er (204/203 onward) has no dossier. Not on any page: when Zhao Xie became king (209 or 208), the seat of Dai, the boundary of either Zhao or Dai, and the exact date of Dai's fall inside October-November 205. Disagreement: Chen Yu's conquest of Changshan is 206 on the Timeline page and 205 on three others (205 used). Pages failed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhao_Xie and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xie,_King_of_Zhao (not found); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Er is a poet and was not used; the Battle of Julu, Battle of Jingxing and Zhang Er (Eighteen Kingdoms) pages were opened instead. Pages beyond the three shared hubs: 3 against a budget of 1-2. Gazetteer: all names resolve.
